workflow: CREATE → COMPILE → CONFIGURE → INTEGRATE → EDIT TEST WORLD → RUN → VERIFY → CONTINUE

configure: Create and compile the four Blueprint shells using the listed parents. BP_PlayerCharacter uses PaperZDCharacter; retain its inherited Capsule, CharacterMovement, Sprite and PaperZD Animation component. Add only the documented camera components. Do not add a second movement or animation driver.

Open BP_GameMode → Class Defaults: set Player Controller Class to BP_PlayerController and Default Pawn Class to BP_PlayerCharacter for the Phase 0–2 lab. Open Project Settings → Maps & Modes and select BP_GameInstance as Game Instance Class and the intended gameplay GameMode. These are project assignments, not new classes.

Open IA_Move and set Axis1D. Open IA_Jump and set Boolean with immediate/default press behavior. Open IMC_Player and add A and D mappings to IA_Move (Negate on A), and Space to IA_Jump. These are suggested development controls; do not create later actions yet.
connect: Open BP_PlayerController. Obtain the existing Enhanced Input Local Player Subsystem for the local player, and add IMC_Player once. Retain a typed CurrentBody after possession; clear it on replacement. Do not construct a custom input subsystem.

Add the Enhanced Input action events: IA_Move Triggered forwards its value to the current body; Completed and Canceled clear it. IA_Jump Started forwards press intent, and Completed/Canceled forward release. In this phase the Character entry points may be compiled shells or diagnostic intent logging: the committed jump policy is implemented in Phase 1.

Configure the existing CharacterMovement plane constraint for X/Z gameplay with Y as the constrained axis. Keep capsule collision separate from noncolliding Sprite presentation. Position the camera to observe the plane, not to follow mirrored sprite transforms.

Compile Controller, Character and GameMode after assigning their references. Save All. BP_GameInstance remains a session shell; do not call Phase 3 Profile/WorldState initialization that has not been built.
world: Open L_MovementLab. In World Settings confirm BP_GameMode is the effective GameMode. Add native floor geometry with blocking collision, a ledge and low ceiling for the coming movement tests, and a native PlayerStart on clear supported floor. Use the documented X/Z plane and enough Y collision thickness; no prescribed world coordinates are required.

Do not place an additional auto-possessed BP_PlayerCharacter alongside the GameMode-spawned player. Preserve an open floor section for later combat fixtures. This is a development lab, not an authored final area. Save the map.
run: Open L_MovementLab, choose Play In Editor with the normal player spawn rather than Play From Here, and inspect the World Outliner: one BP_PlayerController possesses exactly one BP_PlayerCharacter. Confirm the intended camera and collision orientation.

Press/release A, D and Space and inspect the routed intent or debug output. Expect one jump-press request per press, signed horizontal values, and cleared values on release. Full movement feel is not a Phase 0 acceptance claim.
failure: Temporarily remove the effective GameMode override or an input mapping, observe the missing spawn/input route, then restore it. Stop on a duplicate pawn or failed cast; do not compensate by placing a second player.
regression: Stop and restart PIE twice. The same map/player/controller assignments must still work without an extra mapping installation or extra pawn.
deferred: BP_GameInstance is intentionally a staged session shell until Phase 3. IA_Jump is connected to an intent entry point now, but launch/buffer/coyote/variable-height behavior becomes active in Phase 1. No Stats, Health, Combat, interaction, session models or test harness is added yet.

existing.change: Add ActionState, implement the single movement/jump intent policy, and configure the inherited PaperZD Animation component.
Replace any Phase 0 intent diagnostics with SetMoveIntent, RequestJump and ReleaseJump calls; clear held intent at blocking boundaries.
Retain signed movement and immediate jump mappings; verify no Hold trigger or duplicate jump binding was introduced.
Keep the original spawn setup and extend the movement obstacle course.

configure: Compile E_ActionState and BPC_ActionState. Open BP_PlayerCharacter → Components → Add → BPC_ActionState and rename the instance ActionState. Do not move velocity/floor integration out of inherited CharacterMovement.

Import/configure T_TestPlayer, create SPR_TestPlayer, assign that sprite to the documented Idle/Move/Rise/Fall/Land test flipbooks, and save them. Static placeholder frames are sufficient to prove state selection; they are not finished animation.

Create AS_Player as the native PaperZD Flipbook Animation Source. In its editor create each current ASQ_Player sequence and assign its corresponding FB_Player clip. Create ABP_Player using AS_Player, compile it, then open the player’s inherited Animation component and set AnimInstanceClass to ABP_Player.
connect: Open BP_PlayerController and route IA_Move to BP_PlayerCharacter.SetMoveIntent, IA_Jump Started to RequestJump, and release/cancellation to ReleaseJump. Resolve the current possessed body, not a placed map actor or stale cached body.

Open BP_PlayerCharacter. Implement one cached movement application, one TryConsumeJumpRequest path, one jump budget and one variable-height cut. Use the existing buffer/coyote/native-floor policy and ExecuteJump launch path; remove any parallel native Jump binding that could issue a second impulse.

Query ActionState before accepting movement/jump as prescribed. On blocking action, death/travel later, or possession loss, clear the stored intent and pending jump/cut state through the same Character cleanup path.

Open ABP_Player. Read movement/floor/rise/fall/landing facts from its owning body and use the current sequences for Idle, Move, Rise, Fall and short interruptible Land. The AnimBP never calls the gameplay jump or becomes a second movement clock. Compile both modified owners.
world: Open L_MovementLab and preserve the Phase 0 floor, PlayerStart and camera. Add short/long jump gaps, a walk-off ledge, low ceiling and landing floor at meaningful distances for the current tuning. Keep their blocking collision on the same gameplay plane.
Leave a clear side section unused for Phase 2 dummy/hazard tests. Do not add traversal fixtures that require double jump, dash, wall traversal or ledge traversal. Save the map.
run: PIE from L_MovementLab. Test starting, stopping, reversing and airborne steering; then compare a tap jump with a held jump. Observe the matching PaperZD states while the capsule follows the same gameplay movement.

Walk off a ledge and press within/outside coyote time. Press shortly before landing to test buffering, including a buffered tap already released before landing. Hit the low ceiling and repeat landing-to-jump without a stuck Land presentation.
Repeat the movement acceptance cases at the documented 30/60/120 frame-rate settings. Record expected versus observed behavior and tuning; do not infer timing correctness from a single run.
failure: Press jump repeatedly while already airborne, hold the key across landing, and release after a ceiling hit. Verify no extra jump impulse, no repeated cut and no free rearm before a real floor/mode transition.
Block/clear input and re-enable it; the old held axis or buffered jump must not replay. Temporarily remove an animation clip and verify movement still executes, then restore the assignment.
regression: Restart PIE and verify Phase 0 still produces exactly one possessed player with the same camera and signed input. Changing facing must not mirror the camera or leave the Y plane.
deferred: ActionState has its current movement/permission implementation now; later Attack, hit and death consumers are not yet attached. Do not add Stats, Health or Combat until Phase 2, or future-compatible unapproved traversal mechanics.

existing.change: Add Stats, Health and Combat; retain ActionState; implement BPI_Damageable, explicit body initialization and RequestAttack routing.
Complete Attack/Hit/Dead permission, token and interruption behavior required by Combat; remain the sole action authority.
Route IA_Attack to the ready current body; create and bind the first WBP_HUD only after body readiness.
Add IA_Attack with the development attack key; preserve movement and jump mappings.
Add the Attack/Hit/Death sequences to the existing player Animation Source.
Observe Combat/Health/ActionState for Attack/Hit/Death presentation; preserve movement states and gameplay-independent cleanup.
Keep the movement course and add a separate dummy/hazard combat-test section.

configure: Create/compile the enums, value structs, BPI_Damageable and the data schemas before filling typed component references. Compile BPC_Stats, BPC_Health and BPC_Combat shells, then implement their current-phase contracts. Shell compilation is only a dependency checkpoint, not phase completion.

Open BP_PlayerCharacter → Components → Add: add BPC_Stats as Stats, BPC_Health as Health, and BPC_Combat as Combat. Keep the existing ActionState instance. Compile. In Class Settings → Implemented Interfaces add BPI_Damageable, then compile again.

Create DA_PlayerBaseStats using BPDA_CharacterDefinition and configure the documented base stats (initial MaxHealth 100, AttackPower 10, Defense 0) and AnimInstanceClass ABP_Player. Create DA_Attack_PlayerGroundTest and DA_Attack_PlayerAirTest from BPDA_AttackDefinition; set their grounded/airborne eligibility oppositely and retain the documented provisional timing/query values.

Suggested implementation detail: add CharacterDefinition, GroundAttackDefinition and AirAttackDefinition object-reference properties to BP_PlayerCharacter. In Class Defaults assign DA_PlayerBaseStats, DA_Attack_PlayerGroundTest and DA_Attack_PlayerAirTest respectively. These are proposed property names, not verified game-code fields. Do not assign an idle default into Combat.AttackDefinition: that field describes the current accepted execution.

Open BP_TrainingDummy. Add native Hurtbox query collision plus Stats and Health, implement BPI_Damageable in Class Settings, and use the documented dummy BaseStats and Enemy combat side. It does not need Combat, AI, a persistent ID or rewards. Open BP_Hazard and configure its native Trigger, DamageSpec and positive RepeatInterval; it is a damage source, not a second Health authority.
connect: Suggested implementation detail: create one explicit InitializeCombatBody function on BP_PlayerCharacter and call it from the early lab body setup. Keep gameplay unready until it succeeds. Get the owned component references directly from Components variables: validate CharacterDefinition and attack definitions; pass base stats, zero level growth and an empty modifier array to Stats.Recalculate; initialize Health with that ready Stats reference and its initial capacity; inject the same Stats and ActionState references into Combat. Do not depend on component BeginPlay order or a global discovery scan.

Open BPC_Stats.Recalculate and call the documented BFL_GameRules.CalculateStat with explicit per-stat base/growth/flat/percentage/minimum values. Open BPC_Health.TryReceiveDamage and call BFL_GameRules.CalculateDamage once after validating raw input. These suggested pure function names are the existing reference contract; do not duplicate mitigation in Combat or the Character. EvaluateCondition is a Phase 10 extension, not an early typed function.

Bind Health.OnDamageAccepted/OnDied to the Character adapter and ActionState.OnInterrupted to the matching Combat cancellation path. Accepted damage alone can request hit response/knockback; lethal damage establishes Dead and cancels the matching attack. Clear movement requests and hit queries on interruption. Health keeps current health/death detection; the Character does not duplicate those variables.

Implement BPI_Damageable on the Character: GetCombatSide returns Player; ReceiveDamage validates readiness, forwards the unchanged S_DamageSpec to Health.TryReceiveDamage, and returns S_DamageResult. Health queries Stats for capacity/defense and applies mitigation once. Implement the same forwarding adapter on the dummy with Enemy side. Hazard overlap/repeat calls this interface on supported actors; do not bypass it by directly subtracting health.

Open IMC_Player → add a mapping for IA_Attack (suggested J). Open BP_PlayerController and add the IA_Attack Started event, not an unguarded per-frame Triggered attack. Validate CurrentBody/readiness and call BP_PlayerCharacter.RequestAttack. Suggested implementation detail: RequestAttack selects GroundAttackDefinition or AirAttackDefinition from the actual movement mode, then calls Combat.TryStartAttack(Definition) and returns its result/reason. It never sets an action lock or damage itself.

Combat validates the definition/body/mode, requests ActionState.TryBeginAction, snapshots stats and advances authoritative Windup → Active → Recovery. During the active interval it performs the blocking-aware hit query, normalizes/deduplicates Actors, records each target attempt before BPI_Damageable.ReceiveDamage, and eventually finishes or cancels only its matching token. Include crossed-active-window handling under hitches; do not make notifies necessary for queries or cleanup.

Open AS_Player and assign the documented FB_Player_LandTest placeholder to the new Attack/Hit/Death sequences. Extend ABP_Player with Death → Hit → Attack priority over locomotion. Read current gameplay facts and token/body identity, rather than using animation completion to authorize damage or release actions.

Open BP_PlayerController. After possession and successful InitializeCombatBody, create WBP_HUD with this Controller as Owning Player, retain HUD, supply current Health/Stats, bind once, immediately refresh, and Add to Viewport. Readiness and possession may arrive in either order: both call the same guarded setup check. Unbind the old body before replacing it. Compile all modified consumers and Save All.
world: Open L_MovementLab and preserve every Phase 1 movement obstacle. In the reserved open-floor section drag BP_TrainingDummy from Content Browser into the level. Give it enough clearance for both facing directions and repeated grounded swings. Add another target at a reachable ledge/platform height for the already-committed airborne attack; do not invent a new traversal move.

Place BP_Hazard off the main spawn/movement route so damage and lethal tests are deliberate. Select each fixture and check its documented stats/damage/repeat properties in Details. Keep all query shapes on the X/Z gameplay plane with adequate Y thickness. Dummy Hurtbox must respond to the attack query; hazard Trigger must generate the intended overlaps with the player capsule. Sprite collision stays disabled.

Verify World Settings still resolves BP_GameMode, its Default Pawn still supplies one player, and PlayerStart is outside hazards and blocking geometry. Preserve camera orientation. Save the level. These are development fixtures: retain the movement course, and reproduce this test section in registered SliceA after Phase 3 rather than bypassing area readiness.
run: Open L_MovementLab, Save All, then PIE. Move next to the dummy and press the mapped attack control once. Inspect Combat phase/token and dummy Health before/after. Expected: Windup → Active → Recovery and at most one target attempt/damage result for this swing, even while remaining overlapped.

Start a second swing after recovery: the same target can be damaged again. Attack while jumping using the airborne definition, face the other direction and repeat. With the unchanged suggested player/dummy values, raw damage is 5 + 1 × 10 = 15 before the dummy’s zero defense; record actual values if tuning differs.

Walk into the hazard, then leave and re-enter. Confirm accepted damage arrives through the player interface/Health path and sustained overlaps obey the repeat/acceptance policy, not frame rate. Test interruption during windup, active and recovery.

Apply lethal hazard damage. Expected: Health reports death once, ActionState becomes Dead, current attack/query cleanup completes, and new attack requests fail. Phase 2 recovery is Stop/Play to restart the lab; checkpoints do not exist yet.

Temporarily remove HUD/animation presentation and repeat a nonlethal attack/damage case using component debug values. Gameplay must still work. Restore presentation, then repeat the Phase 1 tap/held jump, coyote, buffer, turn and landing cases.
failure: Attack with a missing definition, during recovery/hit response, while dead, and against an Actor without BPI_Damageable. Requests must fail or skip unsupported targets without partial locks, damage or Accessed None errors. Restore deliberately cleared test references.

Place blocking geometry between attacker and target and verify no through-wall hit. Simulate a coarse update crossing the whole Active interval: the documented query policy must still be evaluated. Deliver an old cancellation/completion token and verify it cannot release a newer action.
Remain overlapped with an invulnerable/rejecting target for one swing. The initial policy records the attempt once even if rejected; that swing must not retry continuously until invulnerability ends.
regression: Re-run single-jump, buffered tap, ceiling, grounded/airborne turning and interrupted Land cases in the unchanged movement course. Check movement request clearing after Hit/Dead and exactly one player after PIE restart.
deferred: S_StatModifier exists and is passed as an empty array now; equipment/passive/effect contributions arrive in Phases 7/8/9, with level growth in Phase 5. WBP_HUD initially shows Health/Stats only; Profile/interaction arrive in Phase 3 and ability panels in Phase 9.

Do not add Interaction, Profile, WorldState, checkpoint recovery, enemy AI, inventory, EquipmentVisuals, Abilities or StatusEffects in Phase 2. Attack ProjectileClass/ProjectileSpeed are Phase 5 extensions; do not add typed projectile references before that class exists.

existing.change: Assign the catalog, construct/retain Profile and WorldState once, and coordinate coherent world operations and travel value handoff.
Replace automatic Default Pawn spawning with guarded registered-area initialization and one explicit ready player spawn.
Add Interaction, receive Profile/model-backed build inputs, and adapt early combat setup into explicit area initialization and cleanup.
Route interaction, register for readiness, bind the new ready body/models and reconnect UI after travel/recovery.
Add IA_Interact only now.
Add target/prompt and currently available Profile views; bind then pull from new sources.
Accept complete Profile-supplied build inputs without inventing future growth/equipment/skills.
Reuse its already working damage fixture unchanged in the registered slice.
Reuse its damage path to exercise live health handoff and checkpoint death recovery.
Retain as an early-phase reference; no longer treat it as a valid unregistered end-to-end gameplay area.

configure: Create/compile the listed value schemas, E_EntryReason, interfaces, model Objects and world Actor shells in creation order. Build only fields whose types exist. E_EquipmentSlot defines exactly Shoes, Belt, Head, Gloves, Top, and Pants; its empty equipped map and the empty inventory/purchase collections reserve later persistent shape; they do not activate equipment or skills yet.

Open DA_GameCatalog and assign CharacterDefinition=DA_PlayerBaseStats, Areas entries matching SliceA/SliceB to DA_Area_SliceA/DA_Area_SliceB, and the validated StartingAreaId/StartingSpawnId. In each Area definition assign its actual L_Slice_A or L_Slice_B World and safe default spawn ID. Optional Attacks lookup may reference the Phase 2 definitions; direct player assignments still work.

Open BP_GameInstance → Class Defaults and assign GameCatalog=DA_GameCatalog. In InitializeSession use Construct Object from Class for BP_PlayerProfile and BP_WorldState, Outer=self, retain typed strong references and explicitly initialize them once. Plain Objects do not receive Actor BeginPlay; GameMode must not recreate them on each map.

Open BP_PlayerCharacter → Components → Add BPC_Interaction, rename Interaction and configure the documented bounded query/radius. Suggested implementation detail: use a native query shape owned by the body or an explicit bounded overlap query from the component; normalize hits to Actors and maintain only nearby candidates. No new Blueprint query-manager asset is needed.
connect: Open BP_GameMode → Class Defaults and set Default Pawn Class=None for registered gameplay areas. Preserve BP_PlayerController as controller class. Register Controller, exactly one AreaRoot and the spawn registry; TryInitializeArea must wait for all prerequisites and bSessionReady, with initializing/initialized guards.

Implement InitializePersistentActors before gameplay readiness. Inject existing WorldState into each PersistentState, validate its authored ID and BPI_PersistentActor adapter, apply the found/default record idempotently and subscribe once. Apply must only change local projection, never replay a reward, switch or death.

Adapt BP_PlayerCharacter.InitializeFromProfile to reuse the Phase 2 setup order: validate/inject current references, rebuild Stats from current supported inputs, initialize Health, initialize Combat/Interaction and presentation, then mark ready. GameMode spawns/initializes/possesses one body and tells Controller to bind. Do not keep a second automatic Phase 2 BeginPlay initializer that refills health after a travel handoff.

Open IMC_Player and map IA_Interact (suggested E). In BP_PlayerController use Started → current body Interaction.TryInteract. RefreshTarget reads GetInteractionInfo without mutation; TryInteract revalidates range/readiness/interface and calls one target Interact. HUD observes OnTargetChanged and pulls PromptText immediately.

Implement BPI_Interactable on BP_InteractableBase, inherited by Checkpoint/Switch/Door. Add PersistentState and BPI_PersistentActor to the persistent children. Checkpoint.Interact asks GI.ActivateCheckpoint; Switch asks GI.CommitSwitchAndTargets; Door projects Opened/collision from WorldState and cannot bypass its switch merely because it has an interaction interface.

Wire BP_AreaTransition to GI.RequestAreaTravel with authored target AreaId/SpawnId. Validate destination before blocking input; suspend old-body mutation and capture health values, then open the resolved area and consume the handoff during ready reconstruction. Actor/component references do not travel.

Wire player lethal events through current GameMode/GI checkpoint recovery, retaining current Profile and WorldState. ActivateCheckpoint chooses recovery location without rolling progression back or silently healing. Recovery uses active checkpoint or validated starting fallback. Compile all modified owners and save both maps.
world: Open L_Slice_A and L_Slice_B. Each uses BP_GameMode, exactly one BP_AreaRoot with its matching AreaDefinition, native blocking floor and authored BP_SpawnPoint instances. Use a safe Start spawn and explicit arrival spawns as needed; IDs must be unique within their area. No placed auto-possessed player remains.

Place BP_RoomVolume instances with unique room identities, query collision and the current AreaRoot reference. Put reverse BP_AreaTransition fixtures at reachable exits. Configure target AreaId/SpawnId in Details; position arrival spawns outside the reverse trigger to prevent immediate travel loops.

In a development section of registered SliceA reproduce the movement course plus BP_TrainingDummy and BP_Hazard. Place BP_Checkpoint on safe reachable floor, a BP_Switch and a BP_Door controlling a shortcut. Assign globally unique stable PersistentId values on their PersistentState components; set switch TargetPersistentIds to the actual door IDs and checkpoint Area/Spawn fields to registered safe destinations.

Use a SliceB door as an unloaded-target test where appropriate, while retaining a playable route independent of that gate. Triggers are query-only; door Blocker supplies blocking collision separately. Save both maps and keep a combined ID/spawn/target log. These are slice/development fixtures, not final world design.
run: PIE from registered L_Slice_A with a deliberately new test session. Confirm session models exist once, area projection finishes before input/AI, one player is possessed, and the first HUD snapshot/prompt is correct.

Interact with the switch and checkpoint, travel A → B → A and observe the opened shortcut and selected checkpoint persist. Verify the unloaded door target reflects the committed record on arrival without replaying the switch.

Take nonlethal hazard damage before normal travel: the new body keeps reduced health. Die after another meaningful world change: recover at the chosen safe checkpoint while retaining that later change. Repeat movement, attack and prompt selection on the replacement body.
failure: Test duplicate root/ID/spawn, unknown AreaId/SpawnId, missing catalog and an unready or vanished interaction target. Reject/report the failing readiness/transaction; do not fall back to an unregistered lab or spawn a second pawn.

Apply a persistent record twice; attempt an already completed operation; leave target range after the prompt appears. There must be no duplicate side effect, stale request or direct persistent mutation from the query.

Open L_MovementLab under the new registered-area GameMode as a deliberate negative check: it is not an initialized gameplay area. Use a preserved early-phase revision for isolated old-lab tests, not a production readiness bypass.
regression: In registered SliceA re-run the Phase 1 movement cases and Phase 2 attack/damage/interruption cases. Travel twice and verify no duplicate HUD/model bindings, auto-heal, stale input or old-body callbacks.
deferred: Disk saving is Phase 4. Inventory entry/character/world/recovery schemas support current session data, but item acquisition activates in Phase 4, full inventory operations in Phase 6, equipment in Phase 7 and skill purchases in Phase 8. Keep unsupported collections empty.
S_RuntimeTravelState carries health now; timed effect/recharge fields are added in Phase 9, not placeholder references to unavailable types. L_SystemTests and its harness do not exist until Phase 11.

existing.change: Connect current Profile/WorldState to immutable save snapshots, a one-writer save queue, validated load/recovery and atomic pickup claims.
Implement the minimal shared acquisition path and supported snapshot import/export; keep later full inventory UI out.
Export/import records, discovery and checkpoint values without live Actor references.
Restore loaded persistent values before registered-area projection and safe recovery spawn.
Create WBP_SaveStatus and wire explicit development Test Save/Test Load/Retry controls to existing coordinator operations; show load failure even with no ready body.
Add the now-available typed Items lookup.
Register the test reward item under its exact ItemId.
Provide the inherited interaction contract to BP_PickupBase without target-specific logic in Interaction.
Add a persistent pickup fixture and preserve the existing shortcut/checkpoint/combat route.
Retain reverse travel and unloaded-record reconstruction checks.

configure: Create/compile BPDA_ItemDefinition, E_ItemKind, S_ItemGrant, S_Reward, S_SaveHeader and BP_SaveGame. Configure DA_Item_TestReward with its documented TestReward ItemId and add it to DA_GameCatalog.Items. Use zero reward XP until Phase 5.

Create BP_PickupBase from the documented parent. Add PersistentState and BPI_PersistentActor while retaining inherited interaction. Set ItemId, positive Quantity and authored PersistentId; this placement ID is not an inventory EntryId or definition ID.
Configure WBP_SaveStatus with current GI as its source. The early screen needs actual Saved/Saving/Failed/dirty state, not a green indicator set when RequestSave was merely called.
connect: Connect Pickup.Interact → GI.TryClaimWorldReward. Validate unclaimed source and all item grants first; use one non-latent, non-reentrant operation to stage/commit Profile acquisition and WorldState.Collected with notifications deferred. Publish complete state and increment one persistent revision only after both agree.

Wire standalone Profile/WorldState commits to the coordinator’s revision/save request path without double-counting GI-deferred transactions. Keep stacking in the single Profile implementation reused by TryAddItem/TryAddItems; the pickup does not edit InventoryEntries itself.

Connect RequestSave → immutable BuildSnapshot → the documented one-writer queue. Run Async Save Game to Slot from the supported custom-event graph (RunSaveIO), not a Blueprint function with a latent node. Completion records the captured revision; an older write cannot mark newer state clean. SaveGame only contains Header/Character/World/Recovery values.

Connect TryLoadProfile to validation of candidate generations before importing either model. Reject unsupported/corrupt data or use the documented valid generation fallback; distinguish missing from invalid saves. Reconstruct registered area and safe recovery through the existing bootstrap, never resume mid-attack or restore a saved Actor pointer.

Suggested implementation detail, development-only fixture: add native buttons labeled Test Save, Test Load and Retry to the existing WBP_SaveStatus. Its request handlers forward to the supplied Controller/GI public RequestSave, TryLoadProfile and RetrySave operations; the widget does not build snapshots or mutate models. Create/bind this view even when a load fails and the session is not ready. No new Input Action, widget Blueprint or harness asset is needed; remove these temporary controls in Phase 10. During these UI tests, Controller shows the cursor and uses Game and UI input mode. A native Return to Gameplay button restores Game Only input, hides the cursor and clears held intent; recreate the temporary test panel on the next isolated test launch.

Suggested implementation detail for a fresh-process load before menus: add a clearly labeled bDevelopmentLoadOnStart Boolean to the existing GI startup setup. Set it explicitly for the test before launch. The load branch calls TryLoadProfile before new-model initialization, discovery commits or automatic saves can overwrite the test snapshot; failure stays unready and displays the retry/error view, with no implicit New Game. The other branch is an explicitly selected new test session. Phase 10 replaces this test-only switch with real menu choices.

Controller creates/retains WBP_SaveStatus, supplies GI, binds its completed save-state notifications, immediately pulls state and Add to Viewport. Ensure a failed save offers a real Retry or acknowledged-unsaved continuation rather than silently claiming success or waiting forever. Compile and Save All.
world: Open L_Slice_A. Place BP_PickupBase within the working interaction range along the established route, outside the spawn/hazard and door blocker. In Details set ItemId=TestReward, Quantity=1 and a unique stable PersistentId such as the documented area/room/pickup naming pattern.

Keep L_Slice_B’s reverse travel and existing persistent target fixtures. Confirm pickup query collision, PersistentState readiness, catalog reference and area/spawn IDs. Record the pre-test Profile/WorldState values and use isolated test save slots/user data, never the developer’s valuable saves.
run: PIE in SliceA: collect the pickup, request it again, travel away/back, and inspect one inventory grant plus one Collected record. Open/close the save view; underlying values must not depend on it.

Click Test Save in the development WBP_SaveStatus controls and observe actual success for the intended revision. Set the explicit development startup selection to load, end the application session and launch a fresh Standalone/test process. Its startup load must validate before new-session writes. Compare entry identity/quantity, world records, checkpoint and safe recovery location; use Retry on a deliberate failure, not implicit New Game.
Earn/claim a persistent change after activating a checkpoint, then die. Recovery retains the later change; it must not call disk load to roll back to checkpoint time.
failure: Attempt a claim with an unknown ItemId, invalid quantity or already-collected ID. Fail without either inventory or world mutation. Corrupt only an isolated test save generation and verify fallback/error, never implicit New Game.

Request another persistent mutation while a save is in flight, then complete the older write. Dirty/newer state must remain pending. Exercise write failure, Retry and acknowledged-unsaved cancellation, including a pending travel/quit request.
regression: Repeat reduced-health normal travel, checkpoint death without rollback, one-time switch projection and Phase 2 combat in registered slices. Confirm loading does not replay pickup actions or duplicate model/UI subscriptions.
deferred: The shared item schema supports minimal acquisition now; immediate consumable use is Phase 6, equipment behavior/typed Appearance is Phase 7, timed effects are Phase 9. Do not add unavailable schema types early. XP rewards remain zero until the Phase 5 curve exists.

Full inventory widgets, final save slots UX and menus are later. Keep the development save/load entry route visibly temporary and do not treat static documentation checks as proof of serialization compatibility.

existing.change: Resolve enemy/reward/level definitions and route ordinary versus unique legitimate-death rewards through the existing coordinator.
Activate TotalXP/derived level/all-crossed skill-point awards using the curve, without replaying awards on import.
Rebuild Stats from cumulative level growth after committed progression changes; do not heal on capacity increases.
Add the Phase 5 ranged active-entry projectile hook without duplicating melee execution or attack timing.
Add ProjectileClass and ProjectileSpeed only now that BP_ProjectileBase exists.
Add Enemies and LevelProgression fields using their current-phase types.
Assign the progression table and melee/ranged definitions; validate their attack references.
Initialize enemy bodies and project unique completion before enabling their AI.
Observe current Profile XP/level/points after binding; rewards do not originate in HUD.
Add ordinary and uniquely identified enemy fixtures to the existing slice acceptance route.
Preserve travel and add a safe ranged/obstruction test lane where appropriate.

configure: Create S_LevelProgressionRow before DT_LevelProgression. Select that exact row structure and author the documented cumulative fixture thresholds/growth/entry awards. Assign the table to DA_GameCatalog.LevelProgression; validate explicit Level ordering rather than row-name enumeration order.

Compile BP_EnemyBase and BP_EnemyAIController before children/data. On EnemyBase add Stats, Health, ActionState and Combat; implement BPI_Damageable. Retain inherited PaperZD Animation. Set AI Controller Class and auto-possession policy for the placed/spawned test enemies, but gate decisions on enemy readiness.

Create AS_EnemyTest, its five sequences and ABP_EnemyTest using the documented placeholder clips. Assign ABP_EnemyTest to both enemy definitions and the inherited Animation component setup. Configure the melee/ranged child EnemyDefinition defaults and the definitions’ Attacks arrays.

Open BP_ProjectileBase and set the native ProjectileMovement UpdatedComponent to its collision root. Configure collision/ignored shooter and the inert initialization path. In DA_Attack_EnemyRangedTest assign ProjectileClass=BP_ProjectileBase and positive ProjectileSpeed; leave the melee definition’s projectile class unset.
connect: InitializeEnemy validates its definition, recalculates Stats, initializes Health, injects ActionState/Stats into Combat, and applies any unique persistent record before enabling AI. The damage interface forwards to Health exactly as the player/dummy adapters do.

AIController possession obtains its controlled enemy and waits for bReady. world: Open L_SystemTests and place/configure BP_ArchitectureTestHarness once for controlled cases. No universal player playground or new map asset is needed.

Open registered SliceA/B and review the retained movement course, dummy, hazard, checkpoint, shortcut, pickup, ordinary/unique enemies, equipment/consumables, ability receiver and NPC fixtures. Confirm stable IDs, definitions, collision, safe spawns and required-route reachability are still coherent.

Open L_Frontend for the end-to-end launch/load path. Retain fixture labels and document which development content must eventually be replaced before a production cook; do not rename/move canonical Content folders to hide references.
run: Run deterministic harness assertions, then the complete first-vertical-slice acceptance in registered areas extended with inventory, equipment, both valid skill specializations, abilities/effects and dialogue. Repeat with relevant UI/presentation absent.

Run the packaged executable in a fresh process: New Game, traverse A/B, mutate progress after checkpoint activation, die, save with actual completion, exit, relaunch and load. Compare persistent values/identities and clean recovery state, not an exact old animation or conversation frame.

Repeat key movement/visual/action tests at documented frame rates and under coarse updates. Record observed failures separately from static documentation/build checks; a compiled Blueprint or successful cook alone is not integrated gameplay proof.
failure: Run isolated bad-data cases: duplicate IDs across maps, missing spawns/executor/definition, malformed skill/level graph, incompatible visual layout, corrupt/unsupported save and failed write. Expect actionable rejection/fallback without partial progress or indefinite blocking.

Test stale body/action/session callbacks, repeated initialization/record application/death, missing widgets/notifies and teardown during accepted execution. No duplicate award, hidden gameplay authority or stale reference may remain.
regression: Use the full validation/checklist suites rather than copying every historic test onto every phase. Required gates include fluid movement, action/health integrity, coherent rewards, persistence/recovery, complete stat rebuilds, skill reachability, effects/recharge handoff and safe modal input.
deferred: This phase validates the committed game; it does not authorize new gameplay features or claim runtime success in advance. Stop expansion until actual integrated and packaged results are recorded. Production content remains separate from test fixtures.

BP_GameInstance.text: Created in Phase 0 and assigned in Maps & Modes; intentionally has no persistent-model consumer yet. InitializeSession/retained Profile and WorldState become active in Phase 3, disk save queue in Phase 4. Keep the early lab independent of future types.

IA_Jump.text: Created/mapped and routed in Phase 0 to a Character request entry point. Full launch/buffer/coyote/variable-height behavior is intentionally implemented in Phase 1; this is not an orphan input or an early native Jump shortcut.

E_EquipmentSlot.text: Created in Phase 3 with exactly Shoes, Belt, Head, Gloves, Top, and Pants for the empty persistent equipped-slot map. No runtime equip command yet; Profile.TryEquip/TryUnequip and all six visible equipment controls/layer bindings activate in Phase 7. Existing Head/Body assets or saves require explicit reviewed migration; see the enum compatibility section. Do not attach a new equipment gameplay component.

S_InventoryEntry.text: Created in Phase 3 as the shape of the initially empty Profile inventory collection. Phase 4 pickup acquisition creates real EntryIds/quantities; Phase 6 completes inventory use/UI. It is never a placed Actor or shared mutable Data Asset.

S_StatModifier.text: Consumed by Stats.Recalculate with an intentionally empty modifier array in Phase 2. Level growth enters separately in Phase 5, equipment sources in Phase 7, purchased passives in Phase 8 and effect handles in Phase 9. Do not invent early equipment/skill data.

BPDA_ItemDefinition.text: Phase 4 supports minimal item acquisition; Phase 6 uses immediate healing, Phase 7 adds typed equipment Appearance once BPDA_EquipmentAppearance exists, and Phase 9 resolves timed effects. Do not create variables of unavailable later-phase types.

BPDA_GameCatalog.text: Create CharacterDefinition and Areas at Phase 3; optional existing attack lookup is allowed. Add Items in Phase 4, Enemies/LevelProgression in Phase 5, Skills in Phase 8, Abilities/Effects in Phase 9, optional Dialogues in Phase 10. Assign its DA_GameCatalog instance to GI; the schema itself is not a spawned manager.

BPDA_AttackDefinition.text: Ground/air player instances are selected by the existing player and passed into Combat in Phase 2. ProjectileClass/ProjectileSpeed are intentionally absent until Phase 5 provides the projectile type. No notify or data object owns execution.

S_RuntimeTravelState.text: GI temporarily retains permitted runtime values while replacing the body. Phase 3 carries health; add effect and ability recharge values in Phase 9. Do not save Actor/executor references, timer handles or old-world deadlines, or replay immediate healing on import.

S_CharacterSave.text: Phase 3 session import/export/recovery can use current supported values. Disk serialization through BP_SaveGame becomes active in Phase 4. Later persistent collections remain empty until their features arrive; the structs do not own live state.

S_WorldSave.text: Phase 3 session import/export/recovery can use current supported values. Disk serialization through BP_SaveGame becomes active in Phase 4. Later persistent collections remain empty until their features arrive; the structs do not own live state.

S_RecoveryData.text: Phase 3 session import/export/recovery can use current supported values. Disk serialization through BP_SaveGame becomes active in Phase 4. Later persistent collections remain empty until their features arrive; the structs do not own live state.

S_AbilityContext.text: Passed from current ready body/Abilities to an inert accepted executor and target adapter. Contains live Actor references; never nest it in a save snapshot or normal-travel handoff.

BP_AbilityBase.text: Compile before BP_Ability_TestPulse. Do not place it or trigger effects in BeginPlay; BPC_Abilities spawns the configured child only after preparation and calls StartAbility explicitly. Guard FinishAbility/CancelAbility against repeated/stale callbacks.

BP_InteractableBase.text: Base implementation may be unavailable/no-op. It supplies inherited Trigger/interface structure to Checkpoint/Switch/Door and Phase 4 Pickup. Place concrete configured children for acceptance, not a base Actor expected to invent an operation.

BP_EnemyBase.text: Melee/ranged children inherit the configured shared components, damage adapter, readiness and legitimate-death cleanup. Concrete definition-driven children are placed; ordinary encounters remain transient and only designated unique placements initialize persistent state.

BP_PlayerProfile.text: GI uses Construct Object from Class with Outer=self, retains a typed strong reference and explicitly initializes once. Never Spawn Actor, wait for Actor BeginPlay or reconstruct a new model on ordinary map travel/death. Inject these existing references into current consumers.

BP_WorldState.text: GI uses Construct Object from Class with Outer=self, retains a typed strong reference and explicitly initializes once. Never Spawn Actor, wait for Actor BeginPlay or reconstruct a new model on ordinary map travel/death. Inject these existing references into current consumers.

BP_GameMode.text: Phase 0–2 lab uses its automatic default player spawn. Phase 3 switches Default Pawn=None and registers AreaRoot/Controller/spawns before persistent projection and one explicit initialized/possessed player. Do not leave both spawn paths active.

BP_PlayerController.text: Install current-phase mapping contexts once, retain current ready body, and route intent to owners. Create current-phase widgets, bind then pull, and unbind old body sources before replacement. Phase 10 frontend can have no pawn; permanent progress never resides in this Controller.

BP_PlayerCharacter.text: Keep inherited PaperZDCharacter composition. Add only phase-current owned components; the generated attachment/assignment tables name them. One explicit setup path grows from the lab into area bootstrap, with Stats before Health and old-body cleanup before replacement.

BP_TrainingDummy.text: Place on open combat floor or a reachable platform in L_MovementLab, then reproduce in registered SliceA after Phase 3. Configure Hurtbox query collision, Stats/Health and the damage adapter. No AI, rewards, Combat or stable persistent ID is required.

BP_Hazard.text: Place away from spawn and required movement path, configure Trigger query collision, neutral DamageSpec and positive repeat interval. Route overlaps/repeats through the target damage interface, with per-target throttling and exit cleanup. Persisting the hazard itself is not required.

BP_AreaRoot.text: Place exactly one per L_Slice_A/B and assign the matching area Data Asset in Details. Register before gameplay readiness; do not equate an unregistered L_MovementLab with a production area. Current room/camera is local; discovery commits to WorldState.

BP_SpawnPoint.text: Place in registered slices with area-local unique SpawnId and facing on supported clear floor, outside hazards and arrival/reverse transition overlap. GameMode validates/registers it before spawning one player; actor labels are not stable destination IDs.

BP_RoomVolume.text: Configure RoomId and AreaRoot on each instance and query-only Trigger collision. Initial post-spawn query plus overlap changes update local room/camera and request idempotent discovery through GI. It is not a saved room Actor pointer.

BP_AreaTransition.text: Author TargetAreaId/TargetSpawnId in Details and configure overlap with the ready player. Revalidate then ask GI.RequestAreaTravel. Author a reverse connection and safe arrival outside its trigger; no direct Level Blueprint teleport or unregistered fallback.

BP_Checkpoint.text: Place on safe reachable floor, configure PersistentId and registered area/spawn destination. Interact asks GI.ActivateCheckpoint; it selects recovery without healing or rolling progress back. Apply the saved active/default presentation without reactivating it.

BP_Switch.text: Assign globally unique PersistentId and actual TargetPersistentIds in Details. Interact asks GI.CommitSwitchAndTargets; targets can be unloaded. Configure a real door fixture and prove the result after traveling to its map.

BP_Door.text: Assign stable PersistentId, separate nonblocking interaction Trigger from blocking passage collision, and author a switch pointing to that ID. ApplyPersistentRecord controls local open/blocking state. Empty capability requirement stays empty until a deliberate Phase 9 fixture; interaction must not bypass the switch.

BP_PickupBase.text: Place the existing class for reward/consumable/helmet fixtures, set catalog ItemId, positive Quantity and a distinct source PersistentId. Interaction requests GI.TryClaimWorldReward. Hide from applied Collected state only; do not grant inventory again during projection.

BP_Enemy_MeleeBasic.text: Use inherited body initialization/components and assign the appropriate EnemyDefinition on the child defaults or validated instance. Configure AI possession/readiness and floor/wall probes; only the ranged active-entry route spawns a projectile. Keep ordinary placement IDs transient unless explicitly configured unique.

BP_Enemy_RangedBasic.text: Use inherited body initialization/components and assign the appropriate EnemyDefinition on the child defaults or validated instance. Configure AI possession/readiness and floor/wall probes; only the ranged active-entry route spawns a projectile. Keep ordinary placement IDs transient unless explicitly configured unique.

BP_EnemyAIController.text: Assign as BP_EnemyBase AI Controller Class with appropriate placed/spawned auto-possession. On possess retain the body and wait for its readiness. Controlled think updates target/movement/attack intent; body/Combat execute. Stop timers/targets on unpossess/death/EndPlay.

BP_ProjectileBase.text: DA_Attack_EnemyRangedTest.ProjectileClass references this class. Combat spawns it once at Active entry, initializes snapshotted damage/shooter/direction/speed while inert, then enables collision/movement. Native ProjectileMovement updates the collision root. Hit/overlap share one consume guard before damage; blocking world consumes without damage.

BP_Ability_TestPulse.text: DA_Ability_TestPulse.ExecutorClass references this child; no placed executor or automatic BeginPlay effect. BPC_Abilities accepts/prepares/spawns/commits before StartAbility. Query/deduplicate once, route damage and world targets deliberately, then finish exactly once.

BP_AbilityTestReceiver.text: Place within reachable test range, assign stable PersistentId and registered Capability.TestPulse requirement, and make Trigger discoverable by the ability query. Implement AbilityTarget plus PersistentActor; accepted operation asks GI.CommitWorldRecord and later projection does not replay the pulse.

BP_NPCBase.text: Place in a safe reachable slice location with NPCId, direct DialogueDefinition and query Trigger. Interact requests Controller.BeginDialogue. Do not inherit enemy AI. Optional local persistent projection is separate from global conversation memory; only add PersistentState/interface when that local record is actually required.

BP_MenuGameMode.text: Assign to L_Frontend World Settings with BP_PlayerController and Default Pawn=None. InitializeFrontend requests MainMenu once after Controller registration; it has no gameplay AreaRoot requirement and does not initialize an extra gameplay body.

BP_ArchitectureTestHarness.text: Place once in L_SystemTests and assign current GameCatalog. RunScenario issues public commands, asserts returned/authoritative values and waits on real completion events. Full movement/collision/player/world/travel tests remain in registered slices or frontend, not a readiness bypass in this map.

BP_SaveGame.text: GI BuildSnapshot constructs the supported Header/Character/World/Recovery values and sends an immutable instance to the one-writer save queue. TryLoadProfile validates candidate generations before replacing both models. Do not store actor/component/UI references or a live authoritative model here.

BFL_GameRules.text: Open BPC_Stats.Recalculate and call CalculateStat with explicit per-stat values; open BPC_Health.TryReceiveDamage and call CalculateDamage exactly once after validating raw input. These suggested pure function names are the existing reference contract. EvaluateCondition becomes active in Phase 10 with S_Condition and explicit Profile/WorldState/capability values. No mutable state, world discovery or actor placement belongs in this library.

BPDA_CharacterDefinition.text: Compile before DA_PlayerBaseStats, which is explicitly assigned to the player and later catalog. BaseStats configures Stats; AnimInstanceClass configures compatible PaperZD presentation. Do not instantiate it as a session model.

BPDA_EnemyDefinition.text: Compile before the melee/ranged instances. EnemyDefinition on the concrete child points to the instance; BaseStats/Attacks/animation/rewards flow through explicit EnemyBase initialization and legitimate-death coordination.

BPDA_AreaDefinition.text: Compile before DA_Area_SliceA/B. Each instance links a stable AreaId to its actual World/default safe spawn and is assigned in both catalog and the matching map root; no arbitrary asset-path construction.

BPDA_SkillDefinition.text: Compile before the registered TestRoot/Branch instances; Profile resolves IDs for both availability and atomic purchase. GrantedAbilityIds remains empty until Phase 9 provides the actual active fixture; UI never becomes the graph rule owner.

BPDA_AbilityDefinition.text: Compile before its explicitly catalog-assigned instance. Runtime components resolve/validate the definition before accepting cost/effect, retaining their own execution or live-handle state rather than mutating shared data.

BPDA_EffectDefinition.text: Compile before its explicitly catalog-assigned instance. Runtime components resolve/validate the definition before accepting cost/effect, retaining their own execution or live-handle state rather than mutating shared data.

BPDA_DialogueDefinition.text: Compile after condition/line/variant structs, create the test instance and assign it to the placed NPC. Controller reads eligible authored variants; it owns the transient cursor, WorldState owns completed flags.

BPDA_EquipmentAppearance.text: Compile before DA_Equipment_TestHelmet; item.Appearance references that instance. Its sequence-to-layer mapping and compatibility/layout rules configure EquipmentVisuals only, never movement, action timing or equipment ownership.

IMC_Player.text: Install once on the local player through Controller. Add Move/Jump at Phase 0, Attack at 2, Interact at 3, Inventory at 6, Skills at 8, AbilityPrimary at 9 and Pause at 10. Do not map unavailable or unapproved actions early. Clear cached intent when removing/blocking the context.

IMC_UI.text: Assign UIConfirm/UICancel and install through Controller’s explicit modal policy. Prove focus and paused-trigger behavior for the chosen Game and UI/focused-handler route; UI Only is not assumed to deliver Controller callbacks. Remove/block competing gameplay actions and avoid double handling.

L_MovementLab.text: Primary integrated environment for Phases 0–2: native PlayerStart/GameMode player setup, movement course, then dummy/hazard. After Phase 3 use registered SliceA/B for full current-game tests; preserve the old lab in an early-phase revision or reproduce its course without bypassing readiness.

L_Slice_A.text: Assign the appropriate Area definition/root, safe authored spawns, rooms and reverse transitions. These are the integrated development environments from Phase 3; preserve and extend the cumulative fixture route. Stable IDs/records survive revisits, not arbitrary actor pointers.

L_Slice_B.text: Assign the appropriate Area definition/root, safe authored spawns, rooms and reverse transitions. These are the integrated development environments from Phase 3; preserve and extend the cumulative fixture route. Stable IDs/records survive revisits, not arbitrary actor pointers.

L_Frontend.text: Assign BP_MenuGameMode and launch real New Game/Load/menu flows. No AreaRoot/player bootstrap occurs here; accepted menu commands enter registered slices through GI. Use this as the final packaged launch entry when configured.

L_SystemTests.text: Place/configure BP_ArchitectureTestHarness for deterministic public-API/value checks. Native GameModeBase is a suggested no-player setup, not an alternative gameplay area initializer. Full player/world/travel scenarios run in registered SliceA/B and frontend.
